heroText: Tbilisi is a dramatic capital of balconies, sulphur baths, hilltop forts and a fast-changing food scene. Start in Old Tbilisi, climb or ride to Narikala Fortress, then cross the Bridge of Peace toward Rike Park and modern river views. Tbilisi International Airport is the main gateway, with transfers east of the centre.

areas.name: Old Tbilisi
areas.text: Old Tbilisi is best for first stays, sulphur baths, balcony streets, restaurants and walks to Narikala.

areas.name: Sololaki
areas.text: Sololaki has historic houses, wine bars and boutique hotels close to Freedom Square and the old town.

areas.name: Vera
areas.text: Vera is a leafy central district with cafes, small hotels and a calmer local rhythm.

areas.name: Vake
areas.text: Vake is upscale and residential, useful for longer stays, parks and restaurants away from the tourist core.

airports.name: Tbilisi International Airport (TBS)
airports.text: Tbilisi International Airport is southeast of the city; taxis, buses and hotel transfers connect it with central districts.

airportTransfer.value: 25-40 min by taxi or transfer to Old Tbilisi
airportTransfer.distance: about 17 km southeast of the centre

stayOverview: Old Tbilisi is the easiest first base, Sololaki adds boutique character, Vera is calmer and cafe-led, and Vake works for longer upscale stays with park access and less tourist traffic.
hotelIntro: Tbilisi rewards staying central because hills and traffic affect short distances. Old Tbilisi and Sololaki suit sightseeing, while Vera and Vake are better for quieter evenings and longer stays.
rentalCars: Do not rent for central Tbilisi; hire a driver or car only for wine regions, mountains and monastery trips.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose the Tbilisi base by repeat journeys: sights, evening food, station access and the airport transfer should all still work.

travelTips.title: Hills
travelTips.text: Keep the Tbilisi plan compact: group nearby sights together and leave enough time for transfers, meals and weather changes.

travelTips.title: Wine
travelTips.text: Use taxis after wine bars and tastings, since Georgia's wine culture is central to evenings out.

travelTips.title: Day trip
travelTips.text: Keep one side-trip day flexible from Tbilisi, then choose it only after checking transport frequency and opening hours.

history.label: 1320s
history.text: In the 1320s, the Mongols retreated from Georgia, and Tbilisi became the capital of an independent Georgian state, once again.
Following the establishment of the Tiflis Governorate (Gubernia) in 1846, Tbilisi became its capital.
Under the national government, Tbilisi turned into the first Caucasian University City after the Tbilisi State University was founded in 1918.
In June 2015, a flood killed at least twenty people and caused animals from the city's zoo to be released into the streets. Politics and administration The status of Tbilisi, as the nation's capital.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Arabic dirhams were brought to Georgia following the Arab conquest in the seventh century, and a mint was founded in Tbilisi that produced coins with inscriptions in both Arabic and Georgian.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: David moved his residence from Kutaisi to Tbilisi, making it the capital of a unified Georgian State, thus inaugurating the Georgian Golden Age.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The city also became an important literary and cultural center, not only for Georgia, but also for the Eastern Orthodox world of the time.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The nation itself maintained a form of "semi-independence" and did not lose its statehood, but Tbilisi would be strongly influenced by the Mongols for the next century, both politically and culturally.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: During this period, many parts of Tbilisi were reconstructed and rebuilt.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Russian Imperial administrators implemented a new Western-style city plan and commissioned new buildings and infrastructure, including roads and railroads connecting Tbilisi to other important cities in the Russian Empire, such as Batumi and Poti.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The main new artery built under Russian administration was Golovin Avenue (present-day Rustaveli Avenue), on which the Viceroys of the Caucasus established their residence.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: It was in the former Viceroy of the Caucasus's palace where the independence of three Transcaucasus nations – Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan – was declared by their respective national councils on 26 to 28.
